title: AI trade on its last leg?

observed_trades.setup: Cut part of the position right out of the gate when it took out the prior day's low on a weak semis/growth day.
observed_trades.quote: cut some net when you took out yesterday's lows
observed_trades.notes: 'net' taken as ticker NET (Cloudflare): later says 'forced out of NET' while still listing NetApp as a holding, so it is not NetApp. Sentence begins 'I came into today right ... out the gate'.

observed_trades.setup: Sold the remainder when price came back to his cost (breakeven).
observed_trades.quote: I took the rest of it off when it came down to my cost
observed_trades.notes: Ticker in the same sentence ('cut some net'). Later summarised as 'forced out of NET' (08:50).

observed_trades.setup: Took some off into strength the day before the gap down.
observed_trades.quote: I did a nice enough job yesterday of taking some off at 1,007
observed_trades.notes: Ticker named two sentences earlier ('STX did not close well'). Price captioned '1,007'.

observed_trades.setup: Cut half at the open when it took out its bounce low.
observed_trades.entry_basis: break of its bounce low at the open
observed_trades.quote: I also ended up cutting half of my STX uh right at the open when it took out its bounce low
observed_trades.notes: Timing words in the quote are 'right at the open'; the passage is the recap of today's actions.

observed_trades.setup: Cut the remainder at the close because STX did not close well; would have been flat on the last shares.
observed_trades.quote: and then I ended up cutting the rest right at the close
observed_trades.notes: Ticker in the same sentence (STX). Later: 'forced out of STX'; 'If I were still holding it, I would be flat on the last of my shares'.

observed_trades.setup: Gave it a chance to bounce off the open, then cut half of the remaining position when it lost its opening print.
observed_trades.size: half of what he had left
observed_trades.quote: I ended up cutting half of HPE when you took off half of what I have left of my HPE when you took out its opening print
observed_trades.notes: Already a reduced position before today ('what I have left'). Still holds the rest (16:54).

observed_trades.setup: Same as HPE: cut half. Worried Dell becomes a failed breakout, giving it wiggle room.
observed_trades.quote: I took off um half of what I had left there. Did the same thing with Dell.
observed_trades.notes: Repeated at 06:23: 'today I had to kind of come on in and and take half of my position off the table'; 'this is one that I own as well'.

observed_trades.setup: Small bounce trade off the 10-day moving average.
observed_trades.quote: I tried TER for a small I 3% position for a bounce trade right off the 10-day

observed_trades.setup: Bounce trade did not work in a weak market; took it off.
observed_trades.quote: I tried it right in here, um and I had to take that TER off
observed_trades.notes: Says it tried to rally a little at the end of the day after he was out.

observed_trades.setup: Short on copper as an insanely crowded trade; failed breakout, expects the base to fail. Would look to add.
observed_trades.quote: I did also short some FCX, as we kind of know, copper
observed_trades.notes: Says he could have shorted the push into 67 but 'came in about 50 cents lower' (so roughly 66.50; fill itself not stated as a number). Repeated at 16:31: 'I took FCX'.

observed_trades.setup: Bought the day before; it held up on a weak day.
observed_trades.stop: on any push tomorrow the stop goes to flat (breakeven)
observed_trades.quote: Surprisingly, I bet I bought yesterday um held up well
observed_trades.notes: 'I bet' decoded as IBIT per the known decode. Mentions 'a four B setup' (caption garble) right after.

observed_trades.setup: Tried Lilly the prior Friday; it did not work. Did not re-buy it yesterday around 1180.
observed_trades.quote: I tried buying it last Friday. Unfortunately, no dice.
observed_trades.notes: Ticker named in the preceding sentence ('give credit to some Lilly'). 'tried buying ... no dice' logged as a failed attempt per the brief; it could also mean the order never got in. He adds he did NOT put any on yesterday ('around 1280 or 1180, excuse me').

observed_trades.setup: Failed attempt in Lilly, no longer held.
observed_trades.quote: I tried buying it last Friday. Unfortunately, no dice. Um I did not put any on yesterday
observed_trades.notes: Exit day not stated (failed attempt from last Friday, 2026-08-14). Same ambiguity as the entry row: 'no dice' may mean no fill at all.

observed_trades.setup: Lists NetApp with HPE and Dell as longs he still holds and may get stopped out of.
observed_trades.quote: before I get stopped out of HPE and Dell and NetApp EOS and then I don't have a
observed_trades.notes: Holding inferred from 'is it a matter of time before I get stopped out of HPE and Dell and NetApp'. The word 'EOS' after NetApp is unresolved (see ambiguous_tickers); no row logged for it.

ambiguous_tickers.context: First action of the day: cut some, then sold the rest at cost; later 'forced out of NET' while NetApp is still listed as held
'before I get stopped out of HPE and Dell and NetApp EOS' - could be a fourth holding (EOSE?) or a garble of 'etc.'
'Surprisingly, I bet I bought yesterday held up well' right before MicroStrategy / Bitcoin comments
